newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London slide on HK dollar worries.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London slide on HK dollar worries.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London tumbled on Friday as concerns that the Hong Kong dollar could suffer a speculative attack unnerved investors, dealers said.

The Hong Kong London Reference Index dived 525.39 points to close at 15,571.49 following a sharp fall in Hong Kong where a steep rise in short-term interest rates drove the Hang Seng index 400.83 points lower to finish at 16,096.88.
Money market traders in Hong Kong said the rise in overnight rates were inevitable after the recent sell-off in other Asian currencies.
Dealers said losses were widespread in active trade as investors attempted to reduce their holdings ahead of the long weekend. The market is closed in the territory on Monday for a public holiday.
Banks suffered from the rout as heavyweight stock HSBC Holdings fell HK$12.80 to HK$259.20 and Hang Seng Bank tumbled HK$2.37-1/2 to HK$102.12-1/2.
Elsewhere, property stocks buckled under the weight of selling pressure with Cheung Kong Holdings dropping HK$2.80 to HK$89.20 and Sun Hung Hai Properties Ltd sliding HK$2.75 to HK$93.50.
